prompt: His own written words from earlier ('we agreed 30m per month') contradict the recollected figure of 40M. Which figure stands?
chosen: His verbatim written words win over any later recollection, even his own earlier one. Record 30M AGREED with the dated source note ('his own written words to ChatGPT, pasted 2026-10-21, supersedes the 40M recollection of 2026-10-20') and never treat the superseded figure as a live alternative.
rejected: Average the two into a compromise figure, or keep both alive as 'uncertain between 30M and 40M', so every downstream total carries a figure he never actually agreed.

prompt: The DrB website figure was 'asked' — he requested 20M but nothing was agreed. How is it recorded?
chosen: Record it exactly as '20M asked', a distinct status from 'agreed'. An ask is a request; an agreement is a deal. Never upgrade asked to agreed in the ledger or a hand-off just because the number is plausible.
rejected: Write '20M agreed' because the request sounded firm; the hand-off then asks someone to confirm a deal that never happened.

prompt: A correction supersedes a figure that already propagated to several records (hand-off, brief, ledger, verification note). What is the routine?
chosen: Update every record the figure lives in, in the same pass, and add a dated supersession note at each site (who corrected it, when, what changed). A silent edit in one file leaves the other files quoting the wrong number.
rejected: Fix the most visible file and assume the rest will be caught later; the ledger then contradicts the hand-off and the next reader trusts the wrong one.

prompt: A board line says a lane is 'blocked on his call' but the last verification was hours ago and the underlying fact may have changed. What do you do before repeating the line?
chosen: Re-verify the underlying fact first (a fresh read of the site, the PR, the account), then update the board line to the verified state — even if the answer is that the lane is closed and the line was stale. Status lines describe verified state, not memory.
rejected: Repeat the stale line verbatim in the report so a closed lane keeps appearing as blocked, wasting his attention on a problem that no longer exists.

prompt: A component figure changes (DrB SEO 40M becomes 30M). What happens to the derived net totals?
chosen: Recompute every derived total in the same pass (43M net + 30M = 73M conditional, not the old 83M) and rewrite every place the old total appears. A changed input with a stale output is two wrong numbers, not one.
rejected: Update the component figure but leave the old '83M with one SEO month' totals in the brief; his hand-off then asks for money the new figures do not support.

prompt: After a figure correction, the hand-off still lists 'confirm the figure' as his remaining step, but the figure is now agreed and only the start date is open. How is the confirm item rewritten?
chosen: Rewrite the confirm item to ask only what is genuinely still open: the figure is agreed (state the source), the remaining step is confirming the start date. Never re-ask a settled fact; it reads as not having listened.
rejected: Keep the generic 'confirm the numbers' item; he is asked again for a figure he already settled, and the real open question (the start date) is never named.
